page.title: Settings
page.allowedHostsHint: Comma-separated host names, besides IP addresses, localhost and *.local.
page.namingHint: Placeholders: {'{'}title{'}'} {'{'}year{'}'} {'{'}season{'}'} {'{'}episode{'}'} {'{'}episodeTitle{'}'} {'{'}channel{'}'} {'{'}date{'}'}; numbers with leading zeros: {'{'}episode:02{'}'}. Parts in [square brackets] are left out when a placeholder in them is empty, e.g. {'{'}title{'}'}[ ({'{'}year{'}'})].
page.folderHint: Empty = recordings stay where they are. Otherwise a path below the recording folder with the same placeholders, e.g. {'{'}title{'}'}/Season {'{'}season:02{'}'} or Films.
page.pushServerHint: ntfy.sh is the public service; if you run your own ntfy server, enter its address.
page.leaveUnsaved: There are unsaved changes. Leave the page anyway?
page.plexUrlHint: Easiest with “Sign in with Plex” below. By hand: the address the box reaches the server at, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:32400 or https://plex.example.org.
page.plexFallbackUrlsHint: Tried in order when the address above doesn't answer — e.g. its home-network address (http://192.168.1.10:32400) next to a domain. Signing in with Plex fills them in; separate several with commas.

tokens.subtitle: For app and API clients — separate from the sign-in password above, and revocable on its own.

error.invalid_timezone: Not a valid time zone name (e.g. "Europe/Rome").
error.forbidden: Only an admin can change this.
error.template_syntax: Brackets don't match: every {'{'} and [ needs its partner, and [ ] can't be nested.
error.template_no_title: {'{'}title{'}'} has to appear, and not only in [square brackets].
error.template_slash: No slashes — the scheme sets the file name only, not folders.
error.template_folder: A folder has to be below the recording folder: no leading /, no empty parts, no ..
error.push_server: An address starting with http:// or https://.
error.push_topic: Letters, digits, - and _ only, at most 64 characters.
error.invalid_url: Enter a full address starting with http:// or https://.

install.title: DreamHub as an app
install.standalone: DreamHub is running as an installed app here.
install.prompt: Put DreamHub on your home screen or desktop: it opens in its own window, without the browser's address bar.
install.ios: In Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. DreamHub then opens full screen like an app.
install.needsHttps: Browsers only offer to install an app over HTTPS, and DreamHub is open over plain http here. On an iPhone or iPad, Share → “Add to Home Screen” works anyway. For Android and desktops, the user guide shows how to put DreamHub behind HTTPS.
install.browserMenu: Use your browser's menu: “Install app” or “Add to home screen”.
